obernants.approximation_semantics: Source-derived scoped relation; finite observations do not establish a general proof.
obernants.assumptions: Finite checks do not establish full annotation normalization or converter action semantics. Installed fixtures include 12 shared vectors (eight accepted, four cycle cases), lengths 64/65 and a 132-token budget-exhaustion case. Exact root error strings and stable one-based indexing are part of the checked observation. Paired syntax is byte-identical; named tests passed twice in debug and twice in release.
obernants.domain: Finite supplied head vectors with in-range heads and lawful matching root labels; shared equality fixtures use nonempty, nonself, exactly-one-root cases and valid annotation forms/inventory. Separate tagged boundary fixtures intentionally violate individual prerequisites. Successful allocation, fixed token registries and no external parser/corpus are assumed.
obernants.observation_scope: Test-only join: one supplied head vector produces two lawful record representations and an independent reachability observation. Calls target the real annotation and conversion gates; neither production gate calls the other. On admitted common-domain fixtures, compare acceptance or first root-unreachable token. On boundary fixtures, assert the distinct exact Result observations. Source-local imported unit tests are separate from the two groupant_ tests.
obernants.operator: For the finite supplied-call universe, the modeled excluded observations include accepting a root-disconnected lawful vector, reporting token 3 instead of token 1 for [3,0,4,3], and claiming both gates share empty/self-head outcomes. The first test samples common-domain exclusions and the second samples boundary exclusions; passing them is not a complement model for every parser input.

obernants.operator: Given a projected accepted/rejected result, retain all lawful fixture vectors and token fields producing it under both actual gates. A rejected first token does not identify the rest of the cycle or lexical fields. Given a boundary error, retain the operation tag and earlier predicates; no unique input is recovered.

obernants.operator: Expanded fixtures must exercise n<=64 walk behavior, larger cheap completion and budget-exhausted BFS while retaining exact results. Length alone does not prove the budget was exhausted; shape and source control flow are needed. The named projection test provides outcomes, and source-local checks cover dispatch internals.
